nota: Words of this language that look borrowed from another language but do not exist there with that meaning, grouped by the language they imitate.

parole.significato: aerobics (a form of exercise, designed to enhance one's cardiovascular fitness, normally performed to music)
parole.testo: Pseudo-anglicism, derived from aerobics. While aerobic exists in English to refer to aerobics, it is an adjective and not a noun.

parole.significato: boxing (a sport where two opponents punch each other with gloved fists)
parole.testo: Pseudo-anglicism, derived from boxing, from English box (“a blow with the fist”).

parole.significato: A young male servant, low-position assistant.
parole.testo: Borrowed from English boy. The sense "ballet dancer" is a pseudo-anglicism.

parole.significato: campsite, camping site, campground, camping area (a place where one or more tents may be pitched for an overnight stay…

parole.testo: Orthographic borrowing from English stop. The sense "hitchhike" is a pseudo-anglicism.
Borrowed from French smoking, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English smoking jacket.
First attested in 1777. Pseudo-Latinism, borrowed from German Frisur, from French frisure, with ending Latinized based on Latin -ūra.
